title: Mental state examination
stem: Cubicle 12. Mr Jackson, 58, was brought in by a friend who could not reach him for days and found him at home, unwashed, not eating. Take a brief history, perform a mental state examination, and present your findings and plan.
notes:
Checked against the Royal College of Psychiatrists' MSE structure, NICE NG222 (Depression in adults, 2022) and NICE NG225 (Self-harm, 2022).

MSE (your ASEPTIC mnemonic): Appearance and behaviour, Speech, Emotion (mood subjective, affect objective), Perception, Thought (form and content, including suicidal and homicidal thoughts), Insight and judgement, Cognition. Present it structured, then a formulation: likely diagnosis, risk (to self, others, from others, self-neglect), and a plan.

Severe depression with psychotic features (nihilistic or guilty delusions, mood-congruent hallucinations) and self-neglect needs urgent psychiatric assessment; physical causes (hypothyroidism, B12, alcohol, medication, dementia) and physical consequences (dehydration, AKI) must be checked.

Your MSE notes and marking scheme match this. The SAD PERSONS score in your notes appears under 'how to assess risk'; NICE NG225 advises against using risk scales to predict suicide or decide treatment — use a psychosocial assessment instead (see the self-harm station).

steps.label: Brief history
steps.hint: Presenting problem, psychiatric and medical history, drugs and alcohol, social, forensic.

Now.t: Can you tell me what's been happening?
Now.r: [Long pause] …Nothing matters any more. I haven't been out for weeks.
Wake at 3 every morning. Not eating. No energy. Nothing I used to enjoy.

Background.t: Have you had problems with your mood before? Any treatment?
Background.r: After my wife died two years ago. Tablets for a while; I stopped them.
Blood pressure tablets. Haven't taken them lately.
A bottle of whisky a week. Less now, can't be bothered.
Live alone. Retired. My son is in Canada.

Appearance.r: Unkempt, unshaven, stained clothes, thin. Slumped, poor eye contact, slowed movements.

Speech.r: Quiet, slow, long pauses before answering, little spontaneous speech.

Emotion.t: How would you describe your mood?

Perception.t: Do you ever hear voices or see things others can't?
Perception.r: Sometimes a voice says I'm worthless… it's right.

Thought.t: Thought form and content: worries, guilt, beliefs
Thought.r: Believes his insides are rotting and that he caused his wife's death.

Thought.t: Have you had thoughts of ending your life?
Thought.r: Every day. I've thought about the tablets in the drawer.
Thought.mark: Asks directly about suicidal thoughts and plans

Insight.t: Do you think you're unwell? Would you accept help?
Insight.r: I'm not ill. I'm just a bad person. There's no point.

Cognition.r: Orientated. Slow on serial 7s. Recalls 2 of 3.

opts.t: Severe depressive episode with psychotic features (nihilistic and guilty delusions, mood-congruent voice)
opts.mark: Presents a structured MSE and diagnosis

opts.t: High risk: active suicidal ideation with a plan and access to means, self-neglect, lives alone, poor insight
opts.mark: States risk to self and self-neglect

opts.t: Physical checks: bloods (U&E, glucose, TFT, B12), ECG, hydration; urgent psychiatry assessment; consider MHO if he refuses
opts.mark: Plans physical work-up, urgent psychiatry and MHO if needed

opts.r: Psychotic depression with a suicide plan is a high-risk emergency.

qs.a: Mood is reported; affect is observed
wrong: Affect is what the relatives report at home
Mood is only recorded in mania

qs.a: Belief that one is dead or rotting
wrong: Belief of being followed by the police
Hearing a voice commenting on actions

qs.q: Does NICE NG225 support SAD PERSONS to decide discharge?
qs.a: No — do not use risk scales to decide care
wrong: Yes — a score of 7 or more means admission is needed
Yes, for everyone over 45 years old
Only in the ED, not on the wards

qs.q: Organic cause of depressive symptoms to exclude?

wrong: A learning disability from birth or childhood

badge.name: ASEPTIC
badge.flavor: Appearance to cognition, then risk and a plan.

cards.q: Flight of ideas is typical of…

options: An organic cause (delirium, drugs, Lewy body)
cards.why: Auditory hallucinations are typical of schizophrenia.

options: Awareness of illness and need for treatment
Intelligence, judged by the level of education
Memory for recent and remote events, tested formally

cards.q: Mood-congruent psychotic features in depression include…
Risk assessment in self-harm (NICE NG225) should…
options: Be a psychosocial assessment, not a score
Use SAD PERSONS, admitting everyone who scores over 6
Be skipped if the patient is sober
